info.name: REST in Pieces
info.description: A request for every route of REST in Pieces, made from its OpenAPI document. Start the API with `npx @johnmorrisdotca/rest-in-pieces` (it listens on http://localhost:6800), or change the baseUrl variable. `limit` and `seed` are on in each request; switch on any other parameter you need. Sign in with POST /auth/login and put the access token in the token variable for the routes that need one.

query.description: Records per page, 0 to 1000. Aliases: `size`, `length`, `pageSize`.
Records to skip.
One-based page number in pages of `limit`: `page=3&pageSize=20` is `offset=40&limit=20`.
Alias of `limit`, for use with `page`.

An opaque cursor from `metadata.nextCursor` or `prevCursor`. Overrides `page` and `offset`; an empty `cursor=` starts on the first page with cursor links. A cursor used with different filters, sort, `q`, `seed`, `locale`, `messy` or `max` returns 400.
Caps the dataset size to test end-of-data handling. Defaults to every record: 1000, or more after creates with the session on. Alias: `maxRecords`.
Field to sort by. Append `:numeric` to compare as numbers, e.g. `age:numeric`.
`asc` or `desc` (also `reverse`, `rev`, `backwards`, `-1`). Alias: `sortOrder`.
Case-insensitive text search across every field.
`false` returns the bare array instead of the metadata envelope.
Renames the results key, e.g. `rows`.
Selects a repeatable dataset. The same seed always returns the same records.

Which country the data is written for: `en-CA` (English (Canada)), `en-US` (English (United States)), `en-IN` (English (India)), `zh-CN` (Chinese (China)), `pt-BR` (Portuguese (Brazil)), `en-GB` (English (United Kingdom)), `ru` (Russian (Russia)), `de` (German (Germany)), `id` (Indonesian (Indonesia)), `ja` (Japanese (Japan)), `fr` (French (France)), `fr-CA` (French (Canada)), `ko` (Korean (South Korea)), `es-MX` (Spanish (Mexico)), `vi` (Vietnamese (Vietnam)), or `global` (Global mix): every record from a locale chosen by the seed, weighted toward the bigger developer populations, with `country` saying which. `en-CA` is the default. Names, addresses, phone numbers, prices (in the local currency) and country names follow the locale; `ja` adds katakana readings. Field names never change, so `province` and `postal` hold whatever the country uses. `GET /locales` lists them all.

Rewrites a share of values into the ones that break layouts and parsers: null and missing keys, empty and whitespace-only strings, very long strings (120 characters, 2,000 for descriptions), emoji, combining marks and zero-width joiners, right-to-left text, leading and trailing whitespace, numbers at the edges (0, negative, very large, many decimals) and dates at the edges (the epoch, the far future, 29 February). `true` rewrites about 15% of values; a number from 0 to 1 sets the share, so `0.5` rewrites half and `1` every one. Which values change comes from `seed` and each record's position, so the same URL returns the same mess every time. Values keep their type (a string field holds a string, a number field a number, a date field a date in the same format), but while `messy` is on every field except the id may be null or missing, whatever the schema says.

`json` (default), `csv`, `yaml`, `xml`, `ndjson` (one record per line) or `sql` (one `INSERT` per record, into `table=`). CSV, NDJSON and SQL hold the page's records without the metadata. The `Accept` header works too (`text/csv`, `application/x-ndjson`, `application/sql`).
Wait this many milliseconds before responding, up to 10000. A range such as `200-800` picks a wait inside it from the request, seed included, so the same URL always waits the same time.
Send the headers at once and the body in pieces this many milliseconds apart, whatever the format. With `delay`, the whole response takes no more than 10000 ms.
Respond with this status (200–599). 4xx and 5xx return a simulated error.
`true` fails the request; a fraction such as `0.2` fails that share of requests.

Makes this request a protected route, to rehearse sign-in: `required` (or `true`) wants any signed-in account, `editor` the editor or admin role, `admin` the admin role. Without a valid `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` from `POST /auth/login` it answers `401` (`missing_token`, `invalid_token` or `token_expired`, with a `WWW-Authenticate` header), and for a role that is not enough `403` (`insufficient_role`). Fake tokens, not security.

`true` writes contact details and addresses that cannot reach anybody: emails at `example.com`, `example.org` and `example.net` (RFC 2606), URLs on those domains, phone numbers in the ranges regulators keep for fiction (555-0100 to 555-0199 in Canada and the US, Ofcom, Bundesnetzagentur and ARCEP drama numbers in the UK, Germany and France, and `+1 555-01xx` where a country publishes none), card numbers only from the published test numbers, IP addresses only from 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24 and 2001:db8::/32, and every avatar from this API's own `/avatars/{seed}.svg`. Off by default in 2.x, so existing output does not change; it becomes the default in 3.0.
With `format=sql`: the table the `INSERT` statements name. Defaults to the dataset's name. A letter or `_`, then letters, digits or `_`, up to 63 characters.

request.description:
People with name, age, address, city, province, postal code, country and gender, written for the chosen `locale`: Canadian by default. The original REST in Pieces dataset; also served at `/random-names`.

Any other parameter that names a field filters the results: `gender=female`, `province=Ontario,Quebec`, or ranges with `age[gte]=30&age[lt]=40` (`eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`).

request.description:
Validates the body and answers with the new person: the next id after the dataset's last, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and a `Location` header. Fields the server sets are ignored if sent.

By default nothing is stored, so a later read returns the same data as before and the response is what the write would have produced. With the session on (`--session`, `REST_IN_PIECES_SESSION=true` or `createApp({ session: true })`), the change is kept in memory and later reads at the same `seed` and `locale` see it, until `POST /reset`. A session that is full answers `507`.

request.description:
FHIR R4-shaped Encounter resources for the patients in `/patients`: visits, admissions and consultations, a finished one ending after it starts, a planned one after 2026-01-01, a cancelled or in-progress one with no end. `status` is also the simulation parameter, so filter it as `status[eq]=finished` here or `status=finished` on `/fhir/Encounter`. Synthetic: every record is invented, none comes from or is de-identified from a real person or record, and the codes are this project's own lists, not SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD or CPT. For building and testing software only. `GET /fhir/{type}` answers the same data as a FHIR Bundle.

Any other parameter that names a field filters the results: `gender=female`, `province=Ontario,Quebec`, or ranges with `age[gte]=30&age[lt]=40` (`eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`).

- `nickname:person.firstName?blank=15`: `null` in about 15% of records (`15%` works too, written `15%25` in a URL).
- `score:number.normal(70,10,0,100,1)`, `income:number.lognormal(50000,0.5)`, `wait:number.exponential(5)`, `rank:number.zipf(1000,1)`: values that bunch the way real ones do. `normal` and `lognormal` redraw a value outside `min`/`max` up to 20 times and then clamp it.
